entities.summary:
Sony Pictures Entertainment is the film and television production and distribution subsidiary of Sony Corporation, formed when Sony acquired Columbia Pictures in 1989 for $3.4 billion and TriStar Pictures in 1991. Sony Pictures produces major franchise films including Spider-Man and its associated characters (the only Marvel superhero franchise Sony has retained rights to), the Men in Black series, and notable prestige productions.

Sony's acquisition of Columbia marked the beginning of Japanese corporate ownership of a major Hollywood studio — a transaction that attracted U.S. congressional scrutiny and media commentary about the sale of American cultural institutions to foreign buyers. Sony subsequently lost approximately $3.2 billion on the Hollywood acquisition in the early 1990s due to expensive production failures and excessive executive compensation (Jon Peters and Peter Guber received $272 million buyout of their TriStar contracts).

Sony Pictures' digital storage infrastructure suffered one of the most devastating corporate cyber attacks in history when North Korean hackers breached Sony's systems in November 2014, destroying data, leaking embarrassing executive emails, unreleased films, and salary information, and threatening theaters that showed The Interview (a film satirizing Kim Jong-un). The attack demonstrated cyber warfare's potential against civilian infrastructure. Sony Pictures subsequently invested heavily in cybersecurity. The Spider-Man deal with Marvel Studios (2015, allowing Spider-Man into the MCU while Sony retains production rights) is one of Hollywood's most complex IP-sharing arrangements.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sony Pictures' 2014 North Korean cyberattack was the first act of state-sponsored cyber warfare against a civilian entertainment company, establishing that cinema could be a target of geopolitical conflict.
